node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses "[the fact filing_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2026-02-02]", potentially triggering resubmission during the blackout before 9:00am. The source's calendar-date wording and operational-launch wording support competing temporal interpretations that should remain explicit.

The launch-based candidates select 9:00am as the boundary. This has support in da12aecad4e68.u13.2131, but does not independently resolve the relationship between "With effect from 2 February 2026" and "following its implementation", or establish a timezone.

node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2 permits XML/PDF submissions when "hongkong_post_ecert_available_for_event" is true. Availability is not established as sufficient; the stated assumption does not resolve that interpretive gap.
node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba delegates certificate compliance to "ecert_requirement_satisfied". This avoids equating possession with compliance but leaves the required mechanics externally assessed.

The compliance candidates assess the selected channel, method and e-Cert control, not all circular obligations. XML format selection cannot establish compliance with the separately required XML schema.

Direct urgent contact during the blackout is expressly contemplated by da12aecad4e68.u12.1941. Neither that contact nor automatic migration alone establishes an original submission event triggering resubmission.

A report-history trigger records whether a qualifying event existed, not whether a resubmission duty remains outstanding after later performance. Its externally supplied existence predicate must preserve report identity and sufficient history for a false result.

additional_concerns: All twelve required pairs are retained, including both historical CONTEXT pairs. NOT_APPLICABLE concerns the exact typed question; it neither rejects the supported source claim nor establishes the candidate's overall correctness.

Footnote 3 is present in da12aecad4e68.u30.3569. Its markers attach to the XML and PDF options, not the web form. Both permission claims' missing-footnote statements are stale. The XML statement is supported as a listed-method permission; an alternative reading that treats its extracted conditions as exhaustive sufficient conditions is contradicted by the omitted e-Cert requirement.

The separately provided JFIU XML schema is absent. The circular establishes the obligation to follow it, but not its contents. None of the four opaque dependency IDs identifies that schema, and none has a non-null source_hash; no AVAILABLE assessment or invented dependency mapping is justified.

Both compliance candidates expressly exclude XML-schema conformity from their XML facts. Their TRUE results must remain limited to the selected channel, method and e-Cert control. They do not establish full XML compliance or satisfaction of the separate obligation to liaise with JFIU to arrange a technical test. The source does not expressly make successful completion of that test a precondition to each filing.

Footnote 3 requires a Hongkong Post e-Cert without specifying its operational use. The submission-specific supplied-or-used requirement in node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 may implement that requirement, but the packet does not establish the added operational interpretation or establish that possession alone is insufficient. What JFIU instructions define satisfaction of the e-Cert requirement? Those instructions are missing and have no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The prescribed PDF form is missing external material needed to assess the completed-prescribed-PDF classifications. Which prescribed form or specification governs the submission, and which dependency ID identifies it? No supplied mapping resolves this.

The date-only trigger in node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes the portion of 2 February 2026 before 9:00am. The source separately gives a date-effective channel rule, a 9:00am operational launch and resubmission following implementation. The calendar-date and operational-launch interpretations remain distinct; the date-only predicate cannot distinguish that morning's blackout from the launch.

The timestamp candidates choose an inclusive operational-launch boundary. The packet does not expressly state the governing timezone or definitively resolve how the date-effective provision relates to 'following its implementation' at the exact launch instant. What authoritative clarification resolves these temporal classifications? No supplied dependency ID identifies such clarification.

The blackout provision directs urgent filers to contact JFIU. Contact alone does not establish submission of an STR, but an actual submission resulting from that contact must be assessed on its evidence. Do not generalize post-launch channel exclusivity into the blackout or treat migration as a new original submission.

Non-filing events return FALSE in node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb when its licensed-firm scope holds and facts are nonconflicting, whereas the other event candidates place actual filing in scope and return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this domain distinction instead of treating the candidates as equivalent.

The history candidate answers whether a qualifying event existed, not whether a duty remains outstanding after later resubmission. Its existential assessment is supplied externally; the formula does not inspect history. FALSE needs enough historical evidence to exclude qualifying events.

The circular promises JFIU resubmission guidance, but that guidance is absent. Which guidance governs performance of the resubmission duty, and which dependency ID identifies it? Its absence does not erase the expressly stated trigger or make unrelated method permissions relevant to that trigger.

Rule-wide conflict blocking can prevent evaluation even when an alternative method would otherwise suffice. This is a declared runtime policy, not an additional substantive restriction established by the circular. Missing classifications, conflicts and unresolved temporal facts must retain their declared non-Boolean outcomes.

The calendar-date and operational-launch readings of "following its implementation" remain distinct; these pair assessments do not settle that disagreement.

The source supports a 9:00am launch but does not expressly state the governing timezone or resolve exact-boundary inclusion in the resubmission provision. What authoritative JFIU clarification or applicable time convention resolves those points? Any necessary additional authority is absent and has no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The blackout provision in da12aecad4e68.u12.1941 directs urgent submitters to contact JFIU. It does not establish that every email, telephone call or fax constitutes an actual STR submission, nor grant a general post-launch alternative-channel permission. Automatic migration under da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 likewise does not itself establish a new submission event.

Actual STR filing appears in the scope of nodes node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098, node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913 and node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1. Node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb instead puts submission in its result. A licensed actor's nonfiling event can therefore produce OUT_OF_SCOPE versus FALSE. Equivalence requires an established assessment domain that excludes such events.

Node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3 delegates event existence, temporal interpretation, channel classification and sufficient-history assessment to a supplied Boolean. Its executable result is "Result: the fact report_has_postlaunch_other_channel_submission"; the formula does not perform an existential search. Incomplete history without an observed qualifying event must not be treated as an established FALSE. Attribution to the report's responsible entity also requires care when different entities made different submissions.

These typed questions concern historical DUTY_TRIGGER results. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission does not erase an earlier triggering event, while historical TRUE does not establish that the resulting duty remains outstanding. "Declared output convention: TRUE_IS_SATISFIED" must retain the typed meaning of trigger existence rather than compliance.

The XML provision also requires firms to liaise with JFIU as soon as possible to arrange a technical test. The schema claim is supported as an atomic extraction but does not exhaust da12aecad4e68.u14.2439. This additional action remains separate from the trigger questions.

JFIU's promised resubmission guidance in da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 is absent and has no identifiable supplied dependency mapping. Can the guidance and its applicable version be supplied for any assessment of performance or discharge? The source does not make issuance of that guidance a prerequisite to the stated duty.

All four supplied external dependencies have null source_hash values and no identifying metadata. None qualifies as AVAILABLE or can safely be matched to the XML schema, resubmission guidance or timezone authority. Source unit IDs are evidence identifiers, not external dependency IDs.

The declared UNKNOWN, CONFLICT and scope semantics are distinct from the legal trigger conditions. In particular, a conflicting dependency blocks evaluation even if another operand would otherwise determine the Boolean result. These scoped claim checks do not independently validate that runtime policy.

For node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098, the exact executable condition is "[the fact filing_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2026-02-02]". It includes other-channel filings before 9:00am that day. The source separately states "With effect from 2 February 2026" in da12aecad4e68.u3.811 and "upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026" in da12aecad4e68.u13.2131. Preserve competing readings of "following its implementation" rather than treating the date-only and operational-launch candidates as equivalent.

The operational-launch candidates select an inclusive 9:00am boundary. The launch provisions support that interpretation, but the resubmission passage does not expressly settle exact-boundary inclusion or the governing timezone. What authoritative JFIU clarification or time convention establishes the governing timezone and resolves the implementation boundary? That additional authority is absent and cannot be mapped to any supplied dependency ID.

The urgent-contact provision in da12aecad4e68.u12.1941 applies during the blackout. It does not establish that every email, call or fax is an actual STR submission, or create a general post-launch alternative-channel permission. Likewise, automatic migration under da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 does not by itself establish a new submission event.

No quoted trigger provision makes account registration, XML-schema conformity or e-Cert use a prerequisite to triggering resubmission. Adding those conditions would impose unsupported restrictions on the trigger. Their absence from a trigger formula does not establish compliance with the separate submission requirements.

The surrounding XML provision also requires firms to liaise with JFIU as soon as possible to arrange a technical test. That separate action is outside these trigger questions; the schema claim is supported as an atomic extraction but is not an exhaustive account of da12aecad4e68.u14.2439.

These are historical DUTY_TRIGGER questions. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission does not erase an earlier triggering event; conversely, a historical TRUE does not establish an outstanding duty or noncompliance. The declaration TRUE_IS_SATISFIED must be read consistently with the typed meaning of TRUE as trigger existence.

JFIU's promised resubmission guidance in da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 is missing and has no identifiable dependency mapping. The source does not make publication of that guidance a prerequisite to the stated duty.

The runtime's UNKNOWN and CONFLICT rules remain distinct from legal triggering. The source separately says "With effect from 2 February 2026" in da12aecad4e68.u3.811 and "upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026" in da12aecad4e68.u13.2131. The calendar-date and operational-launch readings of "following its implementation" remain distinct; these pair assessments do not settle that disagreement.

The operational-launch candidates use an inclusive 9:00am boundary. The source supports a 9:00am launch but does not expressly state the governing timezone or resolve exact-boundary inclusion in the resubmission provision. What authoritative JFIU clarification or applicable time convention resolves those points? Any necessary additional authority is absent and has no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The blackout provision in da12aecad4e68.u12.1941 directs urgent submitters to contact JFIU. It does not establish that every email, telephone call or fax constitutes an actual STR submission, nor grant a general post-launch alternative-channel permission. Automatic migration under da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 likewise does not itself establish a new submission event.

Actual STR filing appears in the scope of nodes node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098, node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913 and node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1. Node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb instead puts submission in its result. A licensed actor's nonfiling event can therefore produce OUT_OF_SCOPE versus FALSE. Equivalence requires an established assessment domain that excludes such events.

Node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3 delegates event existence, temporal interpretation, channel classification and sufficient-history assessment to a supplied Boolean. Its executable result is "Result: the fact report_has_postlaunch_other_channel_submission"; the formula does not perform an existential search. Incomplete history without an observed qualifying event must not be treated as an established FALSE. Attribution to the report's responsible entity also requires care when different entities made different submissions.

These typed questions concern historical DUTY_TRIGGER results. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission does not erase an earlier triggering event, while historical TRUE does not establish that the resulting duty remains outstanding. "Declared output convention: TRUE_IS_SATISFIED" must retain the typed meaning of trigger existence rather than compliance.

The XML provision also requires firms to liaise with JFIU as soon as possible to arrange a technical test. The schema claim is supported as an atomic extraction but does not exhaust da12aecad4e68.u14.2439. This additional action remains separate from the trigger questions.

JFIU's promised resubmission guidance in da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 is absent and has no identifiable supplied dependency mapping. Can the guidance and its applicable version be supplied for any assessment of performance or discharge? The source does not make issuance of that guidance a prerequisite to the stated duty.

All four supplied external dependencies have null source_hash values and no identifying metadata. None qualifies as AVAILABLE or can safely be matched to the XML schema, resubmission guidance or timezone authority. Source unit IDs are evidence identifiers, not external dependency IDs.

The declared UNKNOWN, CONFLICT and scope semantics are distinct from the legal trigger conditions. In particular, a conflicting dependency blocks evaluation even if another operand would otherwise determine the Boolean result. These scoped claim checks do not independently validate that runtime policy.

Node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine an offer-level promotional connection with an existential component-level gift classification. Their definitions do not expressly bind the qualifying gift itself to the relevant promotion. In a mixed offer, a linked discount and an unrelated gift could satisfy both inputs without establishing the source's gift-promotion connection. Retain both possibilities: the offer definition may establish that connection for every included benefit, or a same-component link is missing.

The circular defines distributors as intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2, supporting that local context. Paragraph 3.11 is nevertheless quoted in terms of investment products generally. Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f expressly narrows the promoted product to SFC-authorised funds. That may fit this circular's selected context but cannot be assumed to implement the full Code provision.

Node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 uses provider terminology, whereas node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b explicitly attributes the offer to the distributor independently of funding or fulfilment. The operative source concerns who offers the gift. If provider is interpreted as payer or fulfiller rather than offeror, the former candidate could impose an unsupported actor restriction; the supplied definition partly mitigates this by also requiring that the provider offers the component.

The supplied source supports a discount exception for the assessed gift, not permission for a separate non-discount gift accompanying a discount. It also says guaranteed returns or incentives may be gifts, not that they always are. Substantive gift, discount and promotional-link classifications remain judgment inputs; the formulas do not resolve them.

The full Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQ issued on 30 September 2010, identified in db43e253bea18.u29.8110, are missing external authorities for independently resolving contested gift and product-type interpretations. Can their applicable versions be supplied? No dependency IDs are supplied, and circular unit IDs cannot substitute for them.

Both offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift fact. Scope placement changes executable outcomes. node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e places offer occurrence in Scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f, node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 and both offer-level candidates place promotional linkage there. Its absence therefore produces OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than a negative prohibition answer or positive selected-control compliance answer. Preserve the alternatives of an intentionally restricted assessment domain and substantive conditions misplaced in Scope. Unknown scope can also block otherwise decisive result facts.

Both offer-level candidates combine offer-wide promotional linkage with an existential non-discount gift fact. Unless upstream classification connects the same gift component to the promotion, an unrelated gift could be caught merely because another component promotes a product. Negative aggregate answers also require adequate component enumeration and treatment of unresolved classifications; node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not expressly state these evidentiary requirements.

The circular defines distributors through distribution of SFC-authorised funds, while the quoted paragraph 3.11 restriction refers to investment products generally. Candidates differ in their express coverage. Implementing the circular's selected context and implementing the broader Code provision remain distinct alternatives; the latter requires the external Code and an explicit scope decision.

Gift, discount and promotional-link classifications remain supplied judgments. Paragraph 9 says additional returns or incentives may be gifts, not that they invariably are. Absence of structured-product status supplies no gift exemption, and a discount in another component does not exempt a separate gift.

The packet supplies the service description, the gift-classification qualification, the gift restriction and footnote 4. Assertions in the claims that these passages are missing are stale. The external instruments identified by those passages remain distinct from the supplied circular.

For further external-authority review, the packet lacks the Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11, the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010 identified in footnote 3, and paragraph 2.3 referenced by the advertising duty. Their absence does not negate duties expressly stated in the circular. No supplied external dependency IDs exist, and source unit IDs must not be substituted.

The component candidates are not operationally equivalent under the declared runtime semantics. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b place only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also places the offer occurrence in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f places the combined offer-and-promotion fact in scope. A known absence of an offer or promotional link can therefore produce FALSE in one candidate and OUT_OF_SCOPE in another. Unknown scope can also prevent a known non-gift or discount fact from determining the result. The intended question domain must resolve these alternatives.

Both offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift fact. Unless the supplied classifications bind the promotional connection to the same offered component, they may catch an unrelated gift merely because another part of the offer promotes a product. The source connects the gifts themselves to the relevant promotion. Component-linked assessment and aggregation require explicit attribution.

node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 explicitly requires sufficient evidence before finding no qualifying component and retains unresolved classification as unknown. node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not state this evidentiary condition in its aggregate fact definition. The shared UNKNOWN semantics do not themselves prove that upstream component enumeration is complete or that unknown component classifications are supplied correctly.

The source says additional returns or incentives may be considered gifts; it does not classify every guaranteed return or incentive automatically. Gift and discount classifications remain supplied judgments, not implemented legal determinations. The absence of a structured-product finding does not exempt an arrangement from the gift restriction.

The circular defines distributors through distribution of SFC-authorised funds, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 refers to investment products generally. Candidates differ in how explicitly they preserve the circular's narrower context. Preserve the alternatives of implementing only the selected circular scope and implementing the broader Code provision; the latter needs the external Code text and an explicit scope decision.

The component exception must concern the assessed component itself. A discount elsewhere in a combined offer cannot establish the exception for a separate gift. Conversely, the supplied text does not establish a general prohibition on every additional return or incentive, or an exception based on who funds or fulfils a gift.

FALSE for a prohibition question, TRUE for node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5's selected-control compliance question, and OUT_OF_SCOPE are not general legal permissions. Separate advertising, structured-product and other duties may remain applicable.

The candidates refer to a stated source interval, but the supplied material does not identify concrete assessment dates or the effective versions of the incorporated external authorities. Temporal applicability remains unresolved; no present-day validity conclusion follows from this review.

Scope placement changes observable answers even among candidates with the same question hash. For a known distributor and a known unoffered component, node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b can return FALSE, while node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE. Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f also places the offered-and-linked condition in scope. These are not runtime-equivalent alternatives; the intended distinction between not caught and out of scope needs resolution.

Scope differences also affect incomplete evidence. Under the declared runtime semantics, an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN even where a known non-gift or qualifying discount would make a corresponding unscoped prohibition conjunction FALSE. This is an executable distinction, not evidence that the circular imposes an additional legal restriction.

The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine offer-level promotional linkage with existence of a non-discount gift component. The source says, "If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product". Unless the fact contract establishes that the identified gift participates in the linked promotion, the formula can combine a product-linked component with a different, unlinked gift and overstate the restriction. Whether an offer-wide link suffices remains unresolved.

The offer-level existential facts require complete enough component evidence to support FALSE. Node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 expressly states, "False requires sufficient evidence that no offered component meets both conditions; unresolved classification remains unknown." Node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not expressly state this completeness condition. Its generic UNKNOWN semantics do not themselves implement component enumeration or prevent an incorrectly supplied FALSE.

A fee or charge discount is an exception to the selected gift restriction, not a general permission under the circular. Likewise, node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5's TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT result is confined to the selected gift control. Reading either as overall legality would omit the independently supported advertising and section 103 duties.

The source states that guaranteed returns or other incentives "may be considered a gift" in db43e253bea18.u12.2646. Their classification must remain individual and unresolved where evidence is insufficient. The representations generally preserve this qualification; no automatic gift classification or blanket permission for guaranteed returns follows from these checks.

Node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b distinguishes the offeror from whoever funds or fulfils a benefit. The source's wording "distributors should not offer any gifts" supports focusing on offering rather than receipt. However, it does not independently resolve disputed attribution, agency or third-party arrangements. Those remain classification questions, not implemented conclusions.

The circular defines distributors by reference to intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 uses the broader words "a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product". Fund-specific candidate definitions can fit this circular's selected scope, but their equivalence to the full Code provision outside that scope is not established.

The supplied units do not establish an effective interval for the candidates' stated temporal basis. The explicit date 30 September 2010 identifies the FAQ cited in footnote 3; it is not an effective date for every rule or dependency. Applicable versions and competing temporal interpretations remain unresolved.

The declared global CONFLICT blocking and UNKNOWN propagation are supplied runtime conventions, not requirements derived from the circular. They preserve uncertainty but should not be described as legal prohibitions or permissions.

Scope placement changes executable answers. For a known distributor and an unoffered component, node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE, whereas node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b can return FALSE. Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f similarly places offering and promotional linkage in scope. Whether these cases should be outside assessment or answered as not caught remains unresolved.

Node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 place promotional linkage in scope, returning OUT_OF_SCOPE when it is false. Repeating scope predicates in the result does not produce the typed negative answer. Node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 likewise returns OUT_OF_SCOPE for an unlinked benefit rather than TRUE for satisfaction of the selected gift control.

An unknown scope returns UNKNOWN even when a known non-gift or discount would decide an otherwise unscoped gift formula. This is an observable runtime distinction; the circular does not prescribe these evaluation conventions.

The offer-level candidates combine offer-level promotional linkage with an existential non-discount gift classification. The source states, "If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product". Unless the supplied facts establish that the identified gift participates in the linked promotion, these formulas could combine an unrelated gift with another component's promotional link. Whether the offer-wide relationship establishes the required connection remains unresolved.

Node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 states, "False requires sufficient evidence that no offered component meets both conditions; unresolved classification remains unknown." Node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not expressly impose that completeness requirement. Generic UNKNOWN semantics do not implement component enumeration or validate an externally supplied FALSE.

The circular's distributor definition concerns SFC-authorised funds, while the quoted paragraph 3.11 refers to investment products generally. Fund-specific predicates may fit the circular's application, but their equivalence to the full underlying Code provision is not established.

The source says guaranteed returns or incentives "may be considered a gift" and distinguishes fund returns from distributor top-ups. Automatic gift classification would add an unsupported restriction; treating all guaranteed returns as exempt would add an unsupported permission. The candidates generally leave classification to supplied judgment.

The discount exception and TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT result concern the selected gift control only. Neither establishes overall legality. Conversely, section 103 authorisation or exemption is not a stated gift exception.

Node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b focuses on who offers the component rather than who funds or fulfils it. Offering rather than receipt is supported by the source, but disputed attribution, agency and third-party arrangements remain unimplemented classification questions.

The source packet does not establish the candidates' concrete effective interval. The FAQ date is not an effective date for every rule. Historical applicability and relevant external-authority versions remain unresolved.

additional_concerns: All 12 required pairs are retained. Their NOT_APPLICABLE correspondence findings concern the exact typed questions; they neither establish overall candidate correctness nor authorize removal of the supported structured-product and advertising claims.

The component candidates are not operationally equivalent. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b place offering in the result, while node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e places it in scope. With distributor status true, offering false and no conflicts, the former return FALSE and the latter OUT_OF_SCOPE. node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f similarly places the combined offering/promotion fact in scope. These distinctions require an explicit interface decision; FALSE and OUT_OF_SCOPE must not be treated as interchangeable.

Unknown scope can prevent a determinate result that result-level conjunction would otherwise permit. For example, a known discount cannot resolve UNKNOWN promotional scope in node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f, whereas a false non-discount condition can determine FALSE in a result-level conjunction. These are executable differences, not evidence that the circular prescribes either uncertainty policy.

The offer-level candidates separate the offer's promotional link from the existence of a non-discount gift component. They could overcapture an unrelated gift bundled with a product promotion unless the supplied classifications establish that the same component is offered in the qualifying promotion. Neither aggregation predicate explicitly checks that connection for its existential witness.

The gift candidates depend on supplied substantive classifications. Their formulas do not establish distributor status, gift status, discount status or the promotional link. Paragraph 9 supports preserving uncertainty about incentives and guaranteed returns; it does not establish that every additional return is a gift or that every non-structured-product arrangement is permitted.

node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b states that offer attribution is independent of funding or fulfilment. The circular's focus on offering supports not requiring completed payment or receipt, but it does not fully resolve every third-party funding, fulfilment or attribution arrangement. That broader classification assertion remains unverified.

The circular defines distributors by reference to intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2. Some candidate definitions expressly retain that limitation and others use broader distributor language. Conversely, paragraph 10 speaks of a specific investment product or particular product type. Unknown scope can prevent a determinate result that result-level conjunction would otherwise permit. For example, a known discount cannot resolve UNKNOWN promotional scope in node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f, whereas a false non-discount condition can determine FALSE in a result-level conjunction. The offer-level candidates separate the offer's promotional link from the existence of a non-discount gift component. They could overcapture an unrelated gift bundled with a product promotion unless the supplied classifications establish that the same component is offered in the qualifying promotion. The gift candidates depend on supplied substantive classifications. Their formulas do not establish distributor status, gift status, discount status or the promotional link. Paragraph 9 supports preserving uncertainty about incentives and guaranteed returns; it does not establish that every additional return is a gift or that every non-structured-product arrangement is permitted.

node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b states that offer attribution is independent of funding or fulfilment. The circular's focus on offering supports not requiring completed payment or receipt, but it does not fully resolve every third-party funding, fulfilment or attribution arrangement. The circular defines distributors by reference to intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2. Some candidate definitions expressly retain that limitation and others use broader distributor language. Conversely, paragraph 10 speaks of a specific investment product or particular product type. Whether these definitions coincide within the retained source scope must be established before treating the candidates as equivalent.

The three structured-product disputes remain marked unresolved in the supplied prior evidence, without identified disagreeing dimensions. The present proposals separate direct support for the circular's qualified statement from missing authority for independent statutory verification. If authority assessment is confined strictly to extraction, NONE_DECLARED is the narrower alternative; MISSING here identifies the additional statute required for independent classification, not a failure of source support.

A false combined offering/promotion fact similarly places node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f outside scope. Whether these exclusions are intended domain restrictions or incomplete answers to the stated false_means remains unresolved.

Unknown promotional scope can prevent a determinate result even when a known discount would defeat prohibition in a result-level conjunction. The shared global conflict rule can likewise block a result despite a decisive Boolean condition. These are declared runtime policies, not uncertainty rules established by the circular.

The offer-level candidates place promotional linkage at offer level and gift classification in a separate existential predicate. Unless supplied facts connect the same gift component to the qualifying promotion, an unrelated gift bundled with a product promotion could produce an unsupported prohibition. Conversely, assuming the entire offer establishes that connection requires explicit justification.

The circular defines distributors through intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds, while paragraph 10 uses specific investment products and product types. The candidates vary between broader distributor wording and express SFC-authorised-fund limitations. Their actor and product scopes are not established as equivalent.

Gift status remains a supplied substantive judgment. Paragraph 9 says guaranteed returns and other incentives may be gifts; it does not classify them automatically. Paragraph 5 distinguishes fund return from distributor top-up. Neither structured-product status nor its absence settles the gift classification of either component.

The focus on offering supports not requiring completed payment or receipt. However, node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b's statements about funding, fulfilment and attribution do not establish how every third-party arrangement should be classified. Those attribution questions remain unverified rather than automatically constituting executable defects.

Independent verification of the gift standard requires missing external materials: paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct and the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010, identified by footnotes 2 and 3. Can their applicable versions be supplied? No supplied dependency IDs identify them.

Independent verification of the broader advertising regime requires missing Code of Conduct paragraph 2.3, the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes, and the supplementary FAQs and guidance referenced in footnote 4. Can their applicable versions be supplied? NONE_DECLARED in the advertising checks concerns only the circular's explicit narrow duties.

The advertising antecedent is anchored by paragraph 3 and the preceding marketing discussion. Application to a particular service still requires factual classification. The deposit-parallel claim captures one express duty, not every adjacent restriction concerning deposit-like arrangements, deposit-rate comparisons or savings representations.

The packet supplies no concrete applicability interval or competing date interpretations. The candidates' temporal-basis wording does not establish the applicable assessment date or versions of external authorities.

A TRUE gift-compliance result or FALSE gift-prohibition result establishes no general permission and no compliance with section 103, advertising, disclosure or redemption requirements. Separate statutory and advertising duties must likewise not be inserted as additional gift-prohibition conditions.

Scope placement materially changes answers. node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE for an unoffered component. node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f returns OUT_OF_SCOPE when the combined offering and promotional-link condition is false. The two offer-level candidates return OUT_OF_SCOPE when their promotional scope fails. For an otherwise in-scope distributor, the typed prohibition questions can instead be read to require FALSE in those cases. Retain both the narrower-domain interpretation and the negative-answer interpretation until the assessment domain is resolved.

node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 returns OUT_OF_SCOPE when its promotional link is false, rather than TRUE for satisfying the selected gift control through absence of prohibited conduct. This may reflect an intentional assessment prerequisite, but that domain choice is not settled by the typed question. Its TRUE result supplies no permission under section 103 or the advertising requirements.

Moving offering or promotional conditions into scope also changes UNKNOWN propagation: an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN even when a known non-gift classification or discount would make the corresponding prohibition conjunction FALSE. Candidate equivalence therefore cannot be inferred merely from matching conjunctions on fully known, in-scope facts.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional condition with an existential non-discount gift condition without expressly requiring that the same gift component has the promotional connection. In a mixed offer this could impose an unsupported prohibition. Alternatively, the supplied offer classification may be intended to establish that connection for every relevant component; that interpretation requires an explicit fact definition.

The circular's introductory definition supports an SFC-authorised-fund context, while the quoted paragraph 3.11 uses broader investment-product language. The narrower candidate definitions can fit the circular's context, but cannot establish an exhaustive implementation of paragraph 3.11 outside it.

node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b correctly makes attribution of the offer explicit, but its statements that funding and fulfilment are not prerequisites are not expressly resolved by the supplied source. The source supports focusing on offering rather than receipt; detailed third-party attribution remains unchecked and should not create an unsupported permission or restriction.

The source says guaranteed returns or other incentives may be gifts, not that they automatically are gifts. Classification remains supplied judgment in these representations. The concise non_discount_gift_component fact in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 must not be populated as TRUE solely because an incentive exists, or as FALSE solely because one component is a discount.

The disclosure claim's statement that footnote 1 is not supplied is incorrect for this packet: db43e253bea18.u27.7511 supplies it. The claim captures the absence-of-guarantees disclosure, but the source also requires disclosure that investors may not recover principal. That additional duty should remain separately represented if the disclosure regime is modeled.

The advertising claim is supported within the services context developed in db43e253bea18.u3.792 and db43e253bea18.u20.5257–u22.6374. Extending it to every advertisement or treating every reference to savings as a gift would exceed the supplied claim and source context.

External texts absent from the packet include Handbook Overarching Principles section 6.4; Code of Conduct paragraphs 2.3 and 3.11; the answer to question 1 of the SFC Code of Conduct FAQ issued on 30 September 2010; and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes with their supplementary FAQs and guidance. No supplied dependency IDs identify these texts. They are not necessary to establish the two narrow claims expressly stated in the circular, so the pair assessments use NONE_DECLARED. Their absence prevents independent verification of broader interpretations, exceptions or subsequent changes.

Candidates sharing the component question are not operationally equivalent. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b place only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also places offering in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f also places linked promotion in scope. With a known distributor and a known absence of an offer, the former two can return FALSE while the latter two return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this alternative rather than treating the shared question hash as proof of equivalence.

Scope placement also changes uncertainty behavior. A false non-scope gift predicate can resolve a conjunction to FALSE despite an unknown offer or promotional link, whereas an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN before the result is evaluated. The intended boundary between applicability and a negative answer requires an explicit decision; the source does not specify these runtime states.

The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine offer-level promotional linkage with the existence of a non-discount gift component. Their facts do not expressly require that the same component be offered in the linked promotion. In a mixed offer, the definitions need to establish that connection or retain uncertainty; otherwise unrelated components could be combined to produce an unsupported prohibition.

node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 uses 'provider' for the actor, while node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b expressly attributes the offer to an offeror independently of funding or fulfilment. The source regulates distributors who offer gifts. A provider interpreted only as the funder or fulfiller could identify the wrong actor. Conversely, the supplied passage does not settle every agency or third-party attribution question.

The source says guaranteed returns and other incentives 'may be considered a gift'. Automatic classification of every return, top-up or incentive as a gift would add an unsupported restriction. The component candidates preserve classification as a supplied judgment; the shorter offer-level definition in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 should not be populated through an automatic incentive-to-gift assumption.

The fee-or-charge discount exception concerns the assessed component. A separate discount cannot exempt another gift component. Conversely, failing the gift restriction is not established merely because a benefit is not a discount: gift classification and the requisite offer and promotional relationship remain necessary.

The SFC-authorised-fund limitation is supported as the circular's setting by db43e253bea18.u0.2, while paragraph 3.11 is quoted using the broader term 'investment product'. Narrow fund-specific candidates may fit the selected circular scope; they should not be presented as complete implementations of paragraph 3.11 for all investment products without resolving that scope distinction.

TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT in node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 means satisfaction of the selected gift control only. FALSE in a prohibition candidate and OUT_OF_SCOPE likewise provide no general permission. Offering-document disclosure, misleading-advertising duties and section 103 may remain independently applicable.

The supplied representations declare temporal and conflict-handling semantics, but the packet does not establish concrete operative intervals or provide an executed implementation. These checks assess the quoted expressions only; they do not validate runtime behavior, settle competing temporal interpretations or establish current-law applicability.

Footnote 1 is supplied in db43e253bea18.u27.7511, so the disclosure claim's missing-footnote annotation is stale. The source additionally requires disclosure that investors may not recover principal. That separate limb should remain represented if the disclosure regime is modeled.

Scope placement creates substantive operational alternatives. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b put only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also puts offering in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f puts linked offering in scope. The offer-level candidates and compliance candidate put promotional conditions in scope. Failed conditions can therefore produce OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed negative prohibition answer or affirmative selected-control compliance answer. The assessment universe must resolve whether those conditions are applicability boundaries or substantive elements.

Scope placement also changes uncertainty behavior: an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN before a decisive result predicate can resolve a conjunction or disjunction. The supplied source does not prescribe these computational states. Shared question hashes do not establish operational equivalence.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional link with an existential non-discount gift component without expressly requiring that the same component have the requisite promotional connection. In mixed offers, the supplied classifications must establish that connection; otherwise unrelated facts could produce an unsupported prohibition.

The offer-level phrase 'separately identifiable' must not become an additional exemption for bundled or poorly itemised gifts. The source refers to 'any gifts'. A known caught component can support a positive existential result; a negative result requires sufficient coverage of offered components, and unresolved classifications must not silently become false.

The source regulates distributors who offer gifts. The provider terminology in node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 must retain offer attribution rather than identify only a funder or fulfiller. node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b makes that distinction explicit, but the supplied passage does not settle every third-party or agency attribution question.

Paragraph 9, supplied as db43e253bea18.u12.2646, says returns or incentives 'may be considered a gift'. Automatic classification of every guaranteed return, fund return or top-up as a gift would add an unsupported restriction. Conversely, absence of structured-product status does not exempt an otherwise caught gift.

Candidates sharing the component question are not operationally equivalent. node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b place only distributor status in scope; node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e also places offering in scope; node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f also places linked promotion in scope. With a known distributor and a known absence of an offer, the former two can return FALSE while the latter two return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this alternative rather than treating the shared question hash as proof of equivalence.

Scope placement also changes uncertainty behavior. A false non-scope gift predicate can resolve a conjunction to FALSE despite an unknown offer or promotional link, whereas an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN before the result is evaluated. The intended boundary between applicability and a negative answer requires an explicit decision; the source does not specify these runtime states.

The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine offer-level promotional linkage with the existence of a non-discount gift component. Their facts do not expressly require that the same component be offered in the linked promotion. In a mixed offer, the definitions need to establish that connection or retain uncertainty; otherwise unrelated components could be combined to produce an unsupported prohibition.

node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 uses 'provider' for the actor, while node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b expressly attributes the offer to an offeror independently of funding or fulfilment. The source regulates distributors who offer gifts. A provider interpreted only as the funder or fulfiller could identify the wrong actor. Conversely, the supplied passage does not settle every agency or third-party attribution question.

The source says guaranteed returns and other incentives 'may be considered a gift'. Automatic classification of every return, top-up or incentive as a gift would add an unsupported restriction. The component candidates preserve classification as a supplied judgment; the shorter offer-level definition in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 should not be populated through an automatic incentive-to-gift assumption.

The fee-or-charge discount exception concerns the assessed component. A separate discount cannot exempt another gift component. Conversely, failing the gift restriction is not established merely because a benefit is not a discount: gift classification and the requisite offer and promotional relationship remain necessary.

The SFC-authorised-fund limitation is supported as the circular's setting by db43e253bea18.u0.2, while paragraph 3.11 is quoted using the broader term 'investment product'. Narrow fund-specific candidates may fit the selected circular scope; they should not be presented as complete implementations of paragraph 3.11 for all investment products without resolving that scope distinction.

TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT in node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5 means satisfaction of the selected gift control only. FALSE in a prohibition candidate and OUT_OF_SCOPE likewise provide no general permission. Offering-document disclosure, misleading-advertising duties and section 103 may remain independently applicable.

The supplied representations declare temporal and conflict-handling semantics, but the packet does not establish concrete operative intervals or provide an executed implementation. These checks assess the quoted expressions only; they do not validate runtime behavior, settle competing temporal interpretations or establish current-law applicability.

db43e253bea18.u0.2 defines distributors in the circular's SFC-authorised-fund context, while db43e253bea18.u13.2987 states the gift rule in investment-product terms. db43e253bea18.u12.2646 says returns or incentives may be considered gifts. Incentive or guaranteed-return status alone therefore does not establish gift classification. db43e253bea18.u7.1360 also distinguishes fund return from distributor top-up. The candidates leave substantive classification to supplied judgments; their formulas do not perform that assessment.

The aggregate fact in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 is less explicit about evidence completeness than the aggregate in node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5. A FALSE existential classification requires sufficient evidence that no relevant offered component qualifies. An incomplete component inventory or unresolved classification does not by itself establish FALSE.

The circular states a purpose of avoiding distraction, not a separate prerequisite of proven actual distraction. Its quoted gift rule does not require actual payment, receipt, acceptance or an invitation to the public. Adding any of those prerequisites would create an unsupported permission to offer an otherwise caught gift. Conversely, truthful advertising or section 103 authorisation is not stated to excuse the gift restriction.

Unknown scope also matters: node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns UNKNOWN when offering is unknown even if the component is known not to be a gift, while a result-level conjunction can return FALSE. The same distinction arises for unknown promotional scope and a known discount or non-gift. These candidates are not operationally interchangeable merely because their conjunctions coincide on fully known, in-scope facts.

Both offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift fact. For a mixed offer, this does not expressly establish that the identified gift component itself has the required promotional connection. The aggregation is sufficient if the promotional connection applies to that gift or to every assessed component; otherwise it can add an unsupported restriction to an unrelated gift.

node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 describes the actor as the provider. The source regulates the distributor offering the gift. If provider is used merely as a name for that offeror, no extra condition follows; if it requires funding or fulfilment by that distributor, the formula could exclude an offered gift without source support. node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b makes offer attribution explicit.

The circular's opening defines distributors in the context of SFC-authorised funds, while its paragraph 3.11 summary uses investment-product language. Fund-specific facts are supported within the declared circular scope. Neither extending these candidates beyond that scope nor treating the circular as an exhaustive statement of paragraph 3.11's wider reach is established here.

The supplied paragraph 9 says incentives may be gifts, so guaranteed-return or incentive status alone cannot establish gift classification. The candidates generally retain this distinction. The shorter aggregate definition in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 leaves component classification and completeness of the component inventory to supplied judgment; a FALSE aggregate requires sufficient evidence that no relevant component qualifies.

The source's stated purpose of avoiding distraction does not introduce a separate requirement to prove actual investor distraction. The quoted gift rule likewise does not require actual payment, receipt, acceptance or a public invitation. Adding any such prerequisite would create an unsupported permission to offer an otherwise caught gift.

With a known distributor, unknown offering and a component known not to be a gift, node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns UNKNOWN, whereas the corresponding result-level conjunction in node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b returns FALSE, assuming no conflicting facts. Analogous differences occur when promotional scope is unknown but a discount or non-gift classification is known.

The two offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift classification. Their stated facts do not expressly bind that connection to the same gift component. In a mixed offer, this can impose an unsupported prohibition if the qualifying gift is unrelated to the promoted product. The aggregation can be sufficient if the supplied judgments establish that the promotional connection covers that gift; that condition is not explicit.

node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 uses provider for the regulated actor. If this denotes the distributor making the offer, the terminology adds no condition. If it requires funding or fulfilment by that distributor, it can exclude an otherwise caught offered gift without source support. node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b expressly distinguishes offer attribution from funding and fulfilment.

db43e253bea18.u0.2 defines distributors in the circular's SFC-authorised-fund context, while db43e253bea18.u13.2987 states the gift rule in investment-product terms. Fund-specific scope is supported for this circular; the packet does not establish the complete reach of paragraph 3.11 outside that context.

db43e253bea18.u12.2646 says returns or incentives may be considered gifts. Incentive or guaranteed-return status alone therefore does not establish gift classification. db43e253bea18.u7.1360 also distinguishes fund return from distributor top-up. The candidates leave substantive classification to supplied judgments; their formulas do not perform that assessment.

The aggregate fact in node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 is less explicit about evidence completeness than the aggregate in node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5. A FALSE existential classification requires sufficient evidence that no relevant offered component qualifies. An incomplete component inventory or unresolved classification does not by itself establish FALSE.

The circular states a purpose of avoiding distraction, not a separate prerequisite of proven actual distraction. Its quoted gift rule does not require actual payment, receipt, acceptance or an invitation to the public. Adding any of those prerequisites would create an unsupported permission to offer an otherwise caught gift. Conversely, truthful advertising or section 103 authorisation is not stated to excuse the gift restriction.
